# E0517: operation with an `inout` parameter

An operation takes values, not places. Take the value and return the new one, which the code that performs it assigns.

- Rule: [`handlers.no-inout-parameter`](../../reference/12-effects.md#handlers.no-inout-parameter)
- Reported at: the parameter's name.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0517:2
effect Counter {
  fn bump(inout n: i64)
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
effect Counter {
  fn bump(n: i64) -> i64
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0517_operation_with_an_inout_parameter.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0517_operation_with_an_inout_parameter.lt):

```text
── OPERATION WITH AN `inout` PARAMETER ── E0517_operation_with_an_inout_parameter.lt:2:17  [E0517]

An operation takes `n` by value, not `inout`: take it and return the new value:

  2 │   fn bump(inout n: i64)
    │                 ^

An operation takes values, not places. Take the value and return the new one,
which the code that performs it assigns.

To fix it, take `n` by value and return its new value:

  2 │   fn bump(n: i64) -> i64
    │                  +++++++
```
